newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill two ethnic party followers in Karachi.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill two ethnic party followers in Karachi.

text.p: Unidentified gunmen killed two ethnic activists in the Pakistani port city of Karachi on Friday, doctors and police said.

The two followers of the breakaway Haqiqi faction of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) were shot in the city's eastern Shah Faisal Colony area while travelling to their group's office on motorcycles, ambulance workers said.
"It was a planned attack," Haqiqi spokesman Younus Khan said.

The MQM, which is has long been involved in a bloody feud with the Haqibi, is a political ally of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party and a partner in the PML-led coalition government in Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital.
Haqiqi, which was routed in elections on February 3, says that more than 20 of its members have been killed by its rivals since January. The MQM denies the charge and blames the Haqiqi for violence.
The MQM speaks for the Urdu-speaking people who migrated from India in 1947 and their descendents.
